records.name: Lūcija
records.facts_used: Lūcija: The family leads to Roman Lucius, related to Latin lux, light. Lucia is a feminine form, while Lucianus is a derived name in the family. This lexical connection does not establish that a particular child was born in daylight. Siliņš’s dictionary dates the use of Lūcija: 1513. Its calendar year is 1767. This records use of the particular name in Latvia. The entry cannot automatically be transferred to similar spellings or treated as the moment the entire name family originated.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Siliņš p220 Lūcija→Lūcijs and Latin lux; own 1513/calendar 1767. Daylight is a traditional gloss, not an asserted birth circumstance.

records.name: Luciāns
records.facts_used: Luciāns: The family leads to Roman Lucius, related to Latin lux, light. Lucia is a feminine form, while Lucianus is a derived name in the family. This lexical connection does not establish that a particular child was born in daylight. The Latvian Language Agency gives the exact rendering Lucián → Luciāns, citing page 55 of a 1998 manual. This dated record illustrates transmission between languages; it is not a first birth registration or proof of one borrowing route in every family. The dictionary’s 1937 calendar record concerns feminine Luciāna; it is not treated here as a proved date for this masculine name.

records.name: Kastytis

This documents literary use, rather than proving one ancient translation of the name.

records.name: Ere

records.name: Loviise
records.facts_used: Loviise: This form belongs to the Louise/Louis family. Its Germanic base combines hlud or hlut, famous, with wig, battle. Estonian full and short forms also came through German and Swedish, changing their spelling along the way. Page 15 of Mägiste’s 1929 name list gives Loviise as the full form of Lavis; it also recurs under Loovi. This is specific dated evidence for the local form. The dictionary’s publication year is not the name’s invention date or a first birth record.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Original Mägiste PDF p. 17/printed p. 15 Lavis=Loviise andPDF18/printed p. 16 Loovi=Loviise. Exact curated Estonian family and Swedish borrowing dictionary bridge; complete hlud/wig, not only fame.
